evidence.text: The file page identifies ACC-b18630.svg as a digitally created vector of 二 in Western Zhou bronze-script style. It links the rendering to Xiaoxuetang form 33.F82B and names 免簋 (mid-Western Zhou) as the source context. The page says the underlying Sinica database picture is CC0 1.0 and separately marks the Commons file CC0. This is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

evidence.text: The Shuowen entry gives 二 as “地之數也。从偶一” (roughly, the number associated with earth; formed from paired ones). Duan Yucai corrects 偶 to 耦 and explains 耦一 as doubling 一, with two strokes of equal length. This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of the graph’s origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字「二」 - 「說文解字」在線查詢

evidence.field: graphic history, readings, and lexical reconstruction
evidence.text: The entry describes 二 as two parallel strokes and catalogs forms associated with several script traditions, but does not establish a dated earliest inscription or detailed sequence of graphic changes in the inspected material. It lists Mandarin èr (Pinyin), Cantonese ji6 (Jyutping), Middle Chinese Baxter nyijH, Zhengzhang Old Chinese *njis (2003 system), and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *ni[j]-s (2014 system). These concern the spoken numeral, not a phonetic component in the graph.
